clips.title: Use the 3‑Question Test to Spot Real Emergencies
clips.text: Is it urgent? Is it necessary? Is it unexpected? A blown transmission on the only car that gets you to work. Yes, yes, yes, a 65 inch TV on sale for Black Friday. Not urgent, not necessary. And you knew Black Friday existed. That's zero for three. The fund is for the roof leak, the ER visit, the layoff.

clips.title: Why $1,000 Is Your First Emergency Fund
clips.text: $1,000. It feels arbitrary, but it's the line between a bad day and a financial crisis. Picture this. You're driving to work. Hear that thump -thump -thump and pull over to a shredded tire. $400. For a replacement, no buffer. Remember you swipe the credit card, the card carries 24 % interest. You pay the minimum, because rent is due. Six months later, that 400 has become 1200, 1000. In a savings account would have stopped the bleeding at 400. That's the whole point.

clips.title: Automate $25 Each Payday to Build Your Fund
clips.text: Set up a $25 automatic transfer. The day your salary hits, 25 bucks. 26 pay periods. That's $650 a year. You don't decide each time. You don't negotiate with yourself. After a long week, the money Many vanishes before you, can spend it on takeout. Willpower is a battery that drains. Automation is a wire that stays live. If 25 feels tight, start with 10. The habit matters more than the amount, and you can bump it up after a raise.
